summary: Very high compliance. The migration house law (header / prestate with live sha256(prosrc) pins / create-or-replace-only recuts / tail census / preintegration gate module / rig-meta cohort note / gate-chain entry in migration order) is followed to the letter across all three new migrations, and every claim I re-ran (two full db test files, the operation-census+rig-isolation pair, lint, typecheck) matched the tickets' own reports exactly. No applied migration was edited, no PRD/ARCHITECTURE file was touched, the frozen-workflow manifest shows no diff, and no new relation was created (so the FORCE RLS rule does not apply to this diff). Commit-by-commit history is genuinely vertical (test-then-minimal-code per slice); I found no horizontal-slicing anti-pattern anywhere in the 19 commits. Tests exercise the two public doors (clara.list_activity / clara.get_activity_event) rather than an internal collaborator, mocks sit only at system boundaries (HTTP fetch in web unit tests, the e2e HTTP mock), and every vacuity/negative control was shown red for the stated reason before being restored byte-for-byte. Findings below are labelled judgement calls (Fowler smells already present in the surrounding codebase and consistently extended, not introduced) plus one process note about a self-disclosed, self-repaired cross-lane database write; none of them blocks acceptance.

findings.title: Each new activity-feed frontier repeats the same three-function ready/gate/assertCohortPresent triad verbatim, parameterised only by name strings
findings.evidence: Lines 106-192 define `successorLinkReady`/`gateSuccessorLink`/`assertSuccessorLinkCohortPresent` and then `kindLadderReady`/`gateKindLadder`/`assertKindLadderCohortPresent` as two near-identical ~40-line blocks (same shape again in operator-support-fixtures.mjs's `supportTimelineLaneReady`/`gateSupportTimeline`/`assertSupportTimelineCohortPresent`). `grep -rl` over packages/db/tests/*.mjs shows ~30 files already carry this same triad and no shared factory (e.g. `makeFrontierGate(stem, ticketTag, migrationFile)`) exists anywhere in the package.
findings.fix_or_note: A shared helper could collapse ~120 lines of near-identical boilerplate across this diff's three new frontiers into three one-line calls. Not this lane's defect to fix on its own, though: it is a pre-existing, package-wide convention (~30 other files use the identical shape) with no established alternative, and the diff followed the local idiom correctly and consistently rather than inventing a fourth shape. Worth a small standalone refactor ticket against the whole package, not a per-ticket fix.
findings.verdict_note: judgement call, not a hard violation — no documented repo standard forbids the duplication, and the established convention arguably endorses it
